category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.rationale names the digit-counting fallacy concretely ('27 is half-and-half because 2 is even and 7 is odd') and recovery_moves are concrete, but the trap is not anchored to a named research framework or citation. The recovery is a single linear path (cubes -> last-digit rule -> WHY-via-tens) rather than branching by what the diagnostic told you about the child (e.g., 'if child can pair small collections but not articulate WHY, do X; if child can't pair correctly even with cubes, do Y').
category_feedback.required_fix: In expanded_walkthrough.rationale, cite the place-value misconception literature by name (e.g., Ross 1989 'place value as digit-by-digit, not as composed quantity'; or Fuson 1990 on multi-digit number understanding; or Kamii's work on the unitizing required for tens-as-units). Then restructure recovery_moves into two explicit branches: Branch A — child pairs cubes correctly but says '27 is half-and-half'; drill the tens-always-pair-up logic with two-digit numbers first. Branch B — child can't pair cubes correctly even for small N; drop back to 8 vs 9 with physical pairing and one-leftover language before re-introducing the last-digit rule. State which diagnostic signal triggers which branch.
